title: Counting the Months a Micro Market Closure is Charged For
content:
A closure of an Unattended Micro Market Program market that has run at or beyond the minimum suspension printed against its market format is charged by its closed calendar days rather than as one month, and the client's record of approved suspension requests over the trailing year settles which way the part month falls. The closed calendar days are those from the first day of the closure to the day the settlement is raised.

## The clause

1. Where the closure has run at or beyond the minimum suspension printed against the market format, and the agreement carries at or above 2 approved suspension requests over the twelve months to the day the settlement is raised, the closed calendar days are divided by thirty and rounded up to a whole month.
2. Where the closure has run at or beyond the minimum suspension printed against the market format, and the agreement carries below 2 approved suspension requests over those twelve months, the closed calendar days are divided by thirty and rounded down to a whole month, and never below one.
3. Where the closure has run for less than the minimum suspension printed against the market format, no such counting by days is made.

## The boundaries

The repeat closure count is 2 approved suspension requests over the twelve months to the day the settlement is raised: exactly 2 meets it, 1 does not. The closure is measured against the minimum suspension printed against the market format, a closure that has run exactly that many calendar days counting as at or beyond it.

*Hypothetical.* A closure of 47 calendar days on a format whose minimum suspension is 10 calendar days, with 3 approved suspension requests over the trailing year, is charged as 2 months. The same closure with 1 approved suspension request over that year is charged as 1 month. A closure of 47 days with 1 approved request on a format whose minimum suspension is 14 days is likewise charged as 1 month, while a closure of 9 days on that format reaches neither of the first two lines.
